result:
I fixed the five background-work problems. Type-checking is clean, and the job, server and billing tests pass (77/77).

**Root cause:** every job (overdue, digest, retention cleanup, usage recount) took its work list from `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup(N)`. That returned only the N most recently measured orgs, so the same few workspaces were always picked and the rest were never visited. Deleted orgs also reached the overdue sweep, which never checked them.

**Changes:**

- **`src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`**: new `iterateLiveOrgIds(pageSize)`, an async generator that pages through every non-archived org by id (keyset paging).
- **`src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`, `digest-email-job.ts`, `cleanup-archived-job.ts`**: iterate all live orgs via that generator instead of the top-N list. Deleted orgs are now skipped, and per-org behaviour (once-only announcements, digest hour, `markRead`) is unchanged.
- **`src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts`**:
  - `listOrgIdsForRollup(limit)` now lists live orgs (left-joined to their usage row), oldest `measured_at` first, never-measured first, with org id as tie-break. A recount moves an org to the back of the queue.
  - `incrementUsage` no longer touches `measured_at`, so small create/remove deltas don't change queue position.
  - `getUsage` materialises new rows with the epoch as `measured_at`, so an org that has never been recounted sorts to the front.

The usage recount still does 25 per run.
